# Security Hunter Ledger

One line per entry, newest last.

- 2026-08-25 | FIXED | frontend | Dashboard responses missing X-Frame-Options let an attacker page UI-redress a click onto the real Approve/Reject buttons, bypassing the human-in-the-loop approval gate | frontend/trionyx_ui/settings.py
- 2026-08-25 | DOWNGRADED | frontend | `PromptRateLimitMiddleware`/`RequestLoggingMiddleware._get_client_ip` trust a caller-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` header unconditionally (first hop, no proxy validation) — the same class of bug the project explicitly documents and avoids elsewhere (`mcp_server/mcp_server/server.py:148-165`'s `client_ip()`, `lib/tri_onyx/router.ex:1601-1618`'s `extract_source_ip/1`, both of which prefer `CF-Connecting-IP` and never trust XFF). In the default docker-compose topology the frontend is bound to `127.0.0.1:8080` only, so there is no remote attacker today; if it is ever fronted by a reverse proxy for team access, the rate limiter becomes trivially bypassable per-request (spam `/agents/<name>/prompt`, rotating XFF each time) for a cheap cost-amplification DoS against the gateway/LLM spend. Not fixed here because it isn't exploitable in the shipped deployment and downgrading avoided guessing at a proxy topology that doesn't exist in this repo — a human should decide whether to harden it preemptively (mirror the CF-Connecting-IP-or-fail-closed pattern used everywhere else) or leave it since the current bind is loopback-only.
- 2026-08-25 | NO-FINDING | frontend | Reviewed `views/helpers.py` (`render_markdown`, `escape`), `views/chat.py`, `views/builder.py`, `views/approvals.py`, `views/dashboard.py`, `views/graph.py`, `tool_briefs.py`, `schema_cache.py`, `templatetags/ui_filters.py`, `middleware.py`, `gateway.py`, `settings.py`, `urls.py`. Hypotheses tested and killed: (1) `mark_safe(render_markdown(...))` XSS via raw HTML — killed, `html: False` escapes it and no template uses `|safe`/`autoescape off`. (2) markdown link `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:` scheme bypass — killed, `validateLink`'s `BAD_PROTO_RE` blocks case-insensitively. (3) markdown-it-py's `validateLink` bypass via an HTML entity (`&#09;`) hiding a control char inside the scheme, exploitable in raw HTML (`href="java&#09;script:..."` decodes to a real tab, which the WHATWG URL parser strips, executing as `javascript:`) — confirmed the `validateLink` regex bypass exists (it runs on `.strip().lower()` of the string, not per-character, so `java\tscript:` slips past `BAD_PROTO_RE`), but killed end-to-end: `normalizeLink`'s `mdurl.encode` percent-encodes the decoded tab to literal `%09` in the emitted `href`, and a percent-encoded tab is *not* the same as a raw one to the URL parser's tab/newline-stripping step — verified with a headless Chromium page (`element.href` resolves to the inert `java%09script:...`, not `javascript:...`). Not exploitable through this app's pipeline. (4) path traversal in the `/workspace/pages/<commit>/<page_path>` proxy (`views/chat.py:session_page`) reaching files outside the intended set — killed, the frontend passes `page_path` straight through to the gateway's `/pages/:commit/*`, which resolves it via `Workspace.find_commit_file/2` → `git show <commit>:<path>` (an object-tree lookup, not a filesystem join), so `..` segments cannot escape the commit's tree; this is an Elixir-side (repo-store) property, not something the frontend needs to re-validate. (5) `_render_item`/`format_tool_brief` (approvals dropdown) building HTML by hand from agent-controlled tool input — killed, every interpolated field goes through `views/helpers.escape` before insertion.
